newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West next-day cash power quiet, Nov higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West next-day cash power quiet, Nov higher.

text.p: The spot power market in the western U.S. saw little change Tuesday, the second day of a regional schedulers meeting, market sources said.
But cash November prices were slightly higher, despite fading of a recent, largely technical, rally in NYMEX electricity futures.
"A big player was apparently short in both San Juan gas as well as Palo Verde (electricity). But now both are better offered than bid," said one trade source.
He noted that the futures market has been assuming a bigger correlation between Southwest gas prices and electricity than is actually the case.

In addition, recent below-normal temperatures in the Northwest are forecast to rise to the low 60s degrees Fahrenheit later this week and regional precipitation has been well above normal so far this month.
"This bodes well for hydropower generation," noted another trader.

The DC segment of the Pacific Intertie, which runs between the Northwest and California, is scheduled to ramp up to 2,000 megawatts (MW) early Thursday, compared with 1,080 MW currently, but sources said there is a chance that the curtailment could be extended.

Next-day quotes were little changed since most market participants had pre-scheduled through Thursday in preparation for a 2-day information/training meeting held by the Bonneville Power Administration on Tuesday and Wednesday.
California-Oregon border (COB) for Thursday was notionally at $18.50-19.50 per megawatt hour (MWh). Mid-Columbia was quoted $17.50-18.00 and Palo Verde was $18.00-20.00.

Cash November COB was last quoted $19.85-21.10 per MWh, up from $19.40-19.75 on Wednesday. November Mid-Columbia was quoted $18.80-19.10, up from $18.50-18.80, while November Palo Verde was quoted $18.75-19.10, up from $18.40-18.75.
